evidence.excerpt: Dijana Radulović received her Dipl.-Ing. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2004 and 2008 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2013. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2014 and promoted to Associate Professor in 2019 within the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications. Her research group focuses on computational electromagnetic modelling of printed circuit board geometries, signal integrity degradation mechanisms in high-speed mixed-signal designs, and pre-compliance methodologies for reducing radiated and conducted emissions before formal EMC certification. The group makes regular use of a vector network analyser, near-field scanning bench, and FDTD and MoM solvers licensed through the faculty. She teaches courses in Electromagnetic Compatibility and High-Frequency Electronics at both undergraduate and master's level.
